title: What if Space Isn't Empty?
hook: CALAMITY IN PHYSICS! The biggest theory in science has a fatal flaw...

content.main:
For a century, we've described atoms with probability waves and gravity as curved spacetime. These theories work spectacularly well—but they don't connect. Quantum mechanics and general relativity are fundamentally incompatible.

**What if there's a simpler explanation?**

Imagine space not as emptiness, but as an ocean—an incompressible medium called *spation*. When matter exists, it pushes this medium aside, creating pressure gradients.

These pressure gradients are what we experience as forces.

Not gravity. Not electromagnetism. Just pressure.

know-more.title: 🎬 Would you like to know more?
know-more.content:
**Wait, but doesn't this sound like the old ether theory?**

Great question! The 19th century ether was supposed to be the medium for light waves. But experiments like Michelson-Morley couldn't detect it.

Spation is different:
- It's **incompressible**—you can't compress it, only displace it
- It doesn't slow things down—there's no drag
- Light isn't a wave IN spation—it's a pressure disturbance OF spation

**So what's the evidence?**

SDT makes specific predictions that match observations:
- Hydrogen spectrum: <0.1% error
- Planetary orbits: <0.5% error  
- Galaxy rotation: matches without dark matter

16 out of 24 benchmarks validated with errors under 1%.

tech-specs.title: 📊 Technical Details
tech-specs.content:
**The Numbers Behind Spation**

Spation has only two intrinsic properties:

• **Bulk Modulus:** K_bulk = 4.6×10¹¹³ Pa
  (How stiff is space? VERY stiff.)

• **Density:** ρ_s = 5.2×10⁹⁶ kg/m³
  (But this isn't "mass"—it's displacement density)

**Critical Insight:**
There is no gravitational constant G in SDT.
There is no "mass" as a fundamental property.

What we call "mass" is actually a geometric parameter—the amount of spation a particle displaces.

**The Pressure Source:**
All pressure originates from the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) boundary at z = 1089. This isn't just background radiation—it's the structural boundary of the observable universe, pressing inward.

narration.script:
Here's something that might surprise you. The two greatest theories in physics—quantum mechanics and general relativity—they don't work together. At all. They're fundamentally incompatible.

For over a century, physicists have been trying to unify them. String theory, loop quantum gravity, countless attempts. But what if the problem isn't that we haven't found the right combination? What if the problem is the starting point?

What if space... isn't empty?

Imagine space as an ocean. Not of water, but of an incompressible medium. When matter exists in this medium, it pushes it aside. It creates a hole. And around that hole? Pressure gradients.

Those pressure gradients? That's what we call forces. Gravity isn't a curve in spacetime. Electromagnetism isn't a field. They're both just... pressure. Flowing around matter.

Sounds crazy, right? But here's the thing: it works. 16 out of 24 physics benchmarks validated, with errors under 1%.
